parakeet: The version of God being defended only exists within a timeline where the claims of the Bible are true. That a virgin gave birth, that a man rose from the dead, that the sky opened and voices spoke. If those events happened, maybe the belief has a case. But once you find out that timeline never existed, not historically, not scientifically, not credibly, the central reason for belief collapses. You don't just lose belief, you lose the entire scenario that made the belief possible or necessary in the first place. There are no footprints, no voice, no timeline, no John Connor. Just an echo bouncing off the walls of a story that was never grounded in truth. God becomes a sociological gin particle, a phantom idea contingent on a false history sustained by tradition and vaporized by verification, only existing in this sliver of time where tradition was mistaken for truth. Then God is not the conclusion of investigation. God is the starting assumption, smuggled in without scrutiny. And once we inspect that starting point, the virgin birth doesn't hold, the resurrection falls apart, the moral framework cracks, the promise of afterlife fizzle into fear-based marketing. The gods we're being asked to believe in don't exist in the evidence. They don't exist in experience. They only exist in the books that claim them, and only in those books, remove the book and watch the God disappear. Because if Yahweh, Allah, or any other deity existed outside of Scripture, we wouldn't need preachers to defend them. They just exist. So I'm not trying to be edgy. I'm trying to be honest. And the honest truth is you cannot defend a being who doesn't exist without defending the book that made them up. And once that book fails the test, the God goes with it.
